issues.description: Method parameter mismatch for the getter of the boolean attribute 'excellentEnough': the problem/UML requires a public, parameterless getter for the attribute 'excellentEnough' (i.e. a method such as public boolean isExcellentEnough() or public boolean getExcellentEnough()). The solution implementation instead declares a method with a boolean parameter: public boolean isExcellentEnough(boolean strictCheck). Because the implemented method has a parameter, there is no parameterless getter matching the UML/requirements; this will cause tests or student code that expect a parameterless accessor to fail and will confuse students about the required getter signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a parameterless public getter for the boolean attribute 'excellentEnough' that directly returns the field (for example: public boolean isExcellentEnough() { return excellentEnough; } or public boolean getExcellentEnough() { return excellentEnough; }). Remove or keep the parameterized variant only if accompanied by the parameterless getter; tests and the UML mapping should be satisfied by the parameterless accessor.
